records.canonicalEnglish:
Lucia: Have you finished eating already, dear?
Jido: Yes. I'm going with Mamon and the others to investigate the meteor that fell yesterday.
Sion: You're so lucky! I want to see the meteor too!
Lucia: Hee hee... No, Sion. You're still too young.
Jido: Oh, Sion. It looks like I can finally take a day off tomorrow. Shall I take you to see Joe?
Sion: Joe? You mean Uncle Joe, who lives in Dust?
Lucia: Oh, you remember him, Sion? He used to spend a lot of time playing with you.
Sion: Of course I remember! He made all sorts of toys for me out of scrap.
Sion: I like Uncle Joe!
Jido: Joe will be glad to hear that. Well, I'd better get going.

context.speaker: Lucia / Jido / Sion
context.intent: Warm breakfast conversation leading into the expedition and a promised visit.
context.tone: Affectionate adults and an eager child.

records.legacyEnglish: Ten constrained breakfast turns plus Jido farewell in build_demo.py; reviewed directly against the complete source entry.
findings: Existing draft loses Mamon “and the others,” the rarity/tentativeness of Jido's day off, and some affectionate/playful delivery.
“YOU REMEMBER SION?” is an ambiguous vocative. Make the remembered person explicit: “You remember him, Sion?”
The final response means Joe would be happy to hear Sion likes him. Jido then announces his own departure; these are not unrelated stock phrases.
Keep “Uncle Joe” as Sion's familiar address, without asserting biological kinship.

records.canonicalEnglish: Lucia: Sion, you can go out and play, but you are absolutely not to go and see that meteor!

context.speaker: Lucia
context.intent: Allow ordinary play while firmly forbidding the meteor visit.

legacyEnglish.t006:
,
GO PLAY, BUT
STAY AWAY FROM
THE METEOR!

findings: “GO PLAY, BUT STAY AWAY FROM THE METEOR!” retains the main instruction, but canonical English should preserve the explicit permission/firm prohibition contrast.

records.canonicalEnglish:
Shoko: Oh, hello, Sion. That meteor last night was something, wasn't it?
Shoko: Dad said he was going to investigate it this morning, so I asked him to take me along. And he just said, “No!”
Shoko: I'm eighteen, and he still treats me like a child! Honestly!
Shoko: Say, why don't we go together?

context.speaker: Shoko
context.intent: Invite Sion after expressing indignation at her father's refusal.

legacyEnglish.t016:
DAD WENT TO
INVESTIGATE.
I ASKED TO GO.
HE SAID NO.
legacyEnglish.t022:
I'M EIGHTEEN!
HE STILL
TREATS ME AS
A CHILD!

findings: The draft keeps the facts but turns an expressive complaint into a report. Restore the quoted refusal and indignation.
Eighteen is explicit; do not write Shoko as a small child.

records.canonicalEnglish:
Shoko: Then it's settled! What's wrong?
Sion: Well... I was just thinking about all the Gigi in Saxen Canyon...
Shoko: We'll be fine. Look.
Sion: That's a handgun! What are you doing with that?!
Shoko: Hee hee... I just “borrowed” them from Dad's drawer. There are two, so we can protect ourselves.
Shoko: Come on, let's go!

context.speaker: Shoko / Sion
context.intent: Contrast Sion's caution with Shoko's confidence and mischievous weapon reveal.
context.tone: Sion hesitant/alarmed; Shoko teasing and confident.

legacyEnglish.t012:
BUT THERE ARE
SO MANY GIGI
IN SAXEN
CANYON...
legacyEnglish.t034:
I TOOK TWO
FROM DAD. FOR
PROTECTION.

findings: “I TOOK TWO FROM DAD” loses both the drawer and the knowingly euphemistic “borrowed.” This is characterization, not expendable filler.
Do not imply she received permission or that Dad handed the guns to her.
The handgun reveal is an exclamation followed by an alarmed question; retain the reaction across the highlighted item name.

records.canonicalEnglish: Shoko: What? You coward... Some man you are!

context.speaker: Shoko
context.intent: Rebuke his refusal with an explicitly gendered taunt.

legacyEnglish.t004:
YOU COWARD!
SOME MAN
YOU ARE!

findings: Current “YOU COWARD! SOME MAN YOU ARE!” conveys the intended sting. Do not neutralize the taunt or invent stronger abuse.

records.canonicalEnglish: Shoko: Hee hee... Changed your mind? You want to go after all, don't you?

context.speaker: Shoko
context.intent: Tease him when the invitation is revisited.

legacyEnglish.t000:
SO, YOU WANT
TO GO NOW?

findings: “SO, YOU WANT TO GO NOW?” preserves the question but loses her knowing amusement and “after all.”

records.canonicalEnglish: Young man: Hey, Sion. That meteor last night was something, huh? Looks like my dad went to Saxen Canyon with Dr. Penrose and the others to investigate it.

context.speaker: Young man
context.intent: Casual news about the expedition.

legacyEnglish.t010:
DAD WENT WITH
DR. PENROSE TO
SAXEN CANYON
TO STUDY IT

findings: Restore “looks like” and “the others”: the draft makes secondhand news categorical and reduces the group to two people.
The source speaker label is Young Man, not a named character. Dr. Penrose is not a separate new canonical name without cross-checking shared names.

records.canonicalEnglish: Young man: What's wrong? You look pale. Did something happen?

context.speaker: Young man
context.intent: Notice distress and ask about it.

findings: The current draft is a reasonable concise adaptation; canonical restores the opening concern.

records.canonicalEnglish: Old woman: I hear war has finally broken out between the Kingdom of {faction.wyuria} and the {faction.zolias} Empire. What a dangerous world we live in.

context.speaker: Old woman
context.intent: Report war as news she has heard, preserving the state titles.
uncertainty: Romanizations remain unresolved; the source explicitly distinguishes a kingdom and an empire.

legacyEnglish.t003:
WYURIA AND
ZOLIAS ARE
AT WAR NOW.
DARK TIMES.

findings: The draft drops Kingdom/Empire, the reported nature of the news, and the sense that the conflict has finally broken out.
The braces deliberately defer uncertain English spellings to the glossary. Existing WYURIA/ZOLIAS are not official romanizations.

records.canonicalEnglish:
Woman: So much of Hom has been developed now, and it's getting greener. But I hear the area around Hamack, the town to the west, is contaminated with radioactive waste.
Woman: Especially Dust, the waste-disposal site. They say it's full of Gigi that have mutated and become vicious.

context.speaker: Woman
context.intent: Give geographic and environmental context without asserting unreported causes.
uncertainty: Hamack spelling remains provisional; Gigi's exact creature classification remains open.

legacyEnglish.t003:
HOM IS GREENER
NOW, BUT WASTE
POLLUTES THE
HAMACK AREA.
legacyEnglish.t006:
MUTANT GIGI
RUN WILD AT
THE DUST WASTE
DISPOSAL SITE.

findings: Restore radioactive waste, Hamack's western location, development on Hom, and reported rather than firsthand knowledge.
Mutations making Gigi vicious matter; “MUTANT GIGI RUN WILD” is compressed but does not explain the relationship as clearly.
Do not call the development terraforming or say greenery caused the mutations; those mechanisms are not established here.

records.canonicalEnglish: Young woman: It's nice to see so much more greenery lately. But I hear there are lots of large insects breeding near the lake, and it's dangerous out there.

context.speaker: Young woman
context.intent: Welcome the greenery, then warn about prolific large insects.

legacyEnglish.t003:
MORE GREENERY,
BUT HUGE BUGS
NEAR THE LAKE.
IT'S NOT SAFE!

findings: Current text loses the positive opening, breeding, abundance and hearsay; it sounds like a list of facts.
The speaker is labeled a young woman, distinct from the girl in entry 009.
Do not imply the vegetation itself causes monsters.

adaptationAssessment.reason: The current single four-row, 14-cell body cannot naturally retain the positive observation, breeding insects and reported danger. Add display space/pages or narrower rendering rather than reducing the canonical line to fragments.

records.canonicalEnglish: Old woman: Don't go outside town! There are fearsome insects from the canyon roaming the wasteland.

context.speaker: Old woman
context.intent: Give a firm safety warning with the creatures' origin.

legacyEnglish.t004:
STAY IN TOWN!
THE WASTELAND
IS FULL OF
CANYON BUGS.

findings: “CANYON BUGS” can sound like a species name. The source says the insects came from the canyon.

records.canonicalEnglish: Old woman: Your mother? She wandered out of town in a daze, as though something had possessed her.

context.speaker: Old woman
context.intent: Describe observed behavior through a simile, not diagnose possession.

legacyEnglish.t000:
YOUR MOM LEFT
TOWN IN A DAZE
AS IF SHE WERE
POSSESSED.

findings: The existing adaptation largely retains this meaning. Keep “as if/as though” so the comparison does not become an established supernatural fact.

records.canonicalEnglish: Girl: Saxen Canyon? That's the big canyon to the north, isn't it?

context.speaker: Girl
context.intent: Confirm the place being discussed.

legacyEnglish.t003:
SAXEN CANYON?
THE BIG CANYON
UP NORTH?

findings: The draft is close; the full canonical sentence should keep the conversational confirmation.

context.speaker: Old man
context.intent: Speaker label for the conditional elder interactions.

findings: ELDER implies a formal community role that the generic Japanese label does not establish. Prefer Old Man as the canonical label.

records.canonicalEnglish: Old man: You needn't say a word. I understand. Here, take this Camp Kit with you.

context.speaker: Old man
context.intent: Offer equipment with a knowing, reassuring attitude.

findings: “I KNOW” loses the warm implication that he understands without being told.
The source gift does not promise unlimited replacements or specify recovery mechanics.

records.canonicalEnglish: Old man: That meteor seems to have fallen in the canyon north of town. I've lived on Hom for many years, but I've never seen anything like it.

context.speaker: Old man
context.intent: Locate the meteor and stress how extraordinary it is in his experience.

legacyEnglish.t000:
IT FELL IN THE
NORTH CANYON.
I'VE NEVER
SEEN THE LIKE!

findings: Restore “seems,” north of this town, and his long residence on Hom. The draft presents the location as certain and drops the life-experience context.

records.canonicalEnglish: Karu: Sion, your heart rate and perspiration are higher than usual. Are you up to something?

context.speaker: Karu
context.intent: Report physiological changes, then question whether he is plotting something.
context.tone: Measured diagnostic delivery, followed by suspicion.

findings: “PULSE, SWEAT ABOVE NORMAL. PLOTTING?” is a provisional technical abbreviation, not an acceptable canonical voice.
Higher than usual is relative to Sion's usual state; do not turn it into a diagnosis of illness.
The suspicious question can be mildly comic without making Karu accusatory or omniscient.

adaptationAssessment.reason: With SION substituted at the start, the existing four-row/14-cell body and non-clearing wait cannot carry both the complete diagnostic observation and a natural suspicious question. Investigate more display space or narrower Latin text.

context.speaker: Karu
context.intent: Greet Shoko and ask how she is.

findings: “HI!” drops the question. The canonical greeting must retain the friendly inquiry.

records.canonicalEnglish:
Lucia: Oh my, you both look exhausted. What happened? Come over here and rest a while.
[After resting]
Lucia: Off you go, then. Take care!

context.speaker: Lucia
context.intent: Express concern, offer rest, then send them on their way.

legacyEnglish.t001:
YOU BOTH LOOK
TIRED. COME
OVER HERE AND
HAVE A REST.

findings: The existing draft omits her question about what happened.
The farewell is the conventional send-off for someone leaving; it does not mean Lucia herself is leaving.

records.canonicalEnglish: Lucia: There's something odd about you two... You're not planning to go and see that meteor, are you?!

context.speaker: Lucia
context.intent: Voice a strong suspicion as a question.

legacyEnglish.t000:
YOU TWO ARE
ACTING ODD.
GOING TO SEE
THE METEOR?!

findings: The draft communicates the suspicion, but fuller English better preserves the disbelieving, pointed question.

context.speaker: System narrator
context.intent: Item/amount component in the shared discovery message.

findings: KNIFE drops the weapon's identifying qualifier; keep Survival Knife in canonical terminology.

context.speaker: System narrator
context.intent: Item/amount component in the shared discovery message.
uncertainty: Canonical name unresolved; placeholder is intentional.

findings: MEDS is a provisional display label, not a determination that this is loose medicine. Resolve the item's nature before choosing a canonical English name.

context.speaker: System narrator
context.intent: Item/amount component in the shared discovery message.
uncertainty: Canonical name unresolved; placeholder is intentional.

findings: PROTECTOR is a provisional transliteration. Confirm the equipment type before replacing it with a specific armor name.

context.speaker: System narrator
context.intent: Item/amount component in the shared discovery message.

findings: The source amount is 80; keep the number and currency together in the semantic message. The old line split is technical only.

context.speaker: System narrator
context.intent: Complete discovery message composed with the preceding highlighted item or amount.

findings: The source is a suffix. Canonical English describes the complete message, not the fragment “FOUND.”
A natural adaptation may use “{item} found.” The current engine emits the item first; moving “You found” before it is an engineering change, not a text-only replacement.

records.canonicalEnglish:
Lucia: Sion! What are you doing?!
Sion: Tch. She caught me.

context.speaker: Lucia / Sion
context.intent: Catch Sion in the act and preserve his annoyed response.
context.tone: Lucia sharp; Sion annoyed at being caught.

findings: “WHAT'S GOING ON?” is less direct than Lucia's challenge about what he is doing.
“BUSTED.” is a plausible colloquial adaptation of being caught, but the canonical line should retain the irritated reaction.

records.canonicalEnglish: I can't just take someone else's things without asking.

context.speaker: Unlabeled thought; likely player character
context.intent: Refuse to take another person's property without permission.
uncertainty: This entry clears a speaker header rather than naming a speaker; do not claim a voiced Sion line as established.

findings: “NOT MINE. CAN'T TAKE IT” conveys the restriction but loses the permission/moral nuance and sounds mechanical.

records.canonicalEnglish: Oh, it looks like you're carrying too much. Please make some room and come back.

context.speaker: Unconfirmed speaker
context.intent: Politely ask the player to free inventory space before returning.

legacyEnglish.t001:
YOUR BAGS ARE
FULL. MAKE
SOME ROOM.

findings: The current draft is too brusque for the polite request and omits coming back. Do not invent a physical bag-count mechanic.

records.canonicalEnglish: Where on earth have you been?! The woman at the counter was furious!

context.speaker: Unconfirmed speaker
context.intent: Reproach an absence and report someone else's anger.

legacyEnglish.t000:
WHERE WERE
YOU?! THE GIRL
AT THE COUNTER
WAS FURIOUS!

findings: “The girl at the counter” may imply an age not established by the colloquial address. Use woman unless later context identifies her.
Keep the past tense: the line reports how she reacted.

records.canonicalEnglish: Ask the woman at the counter about work.

context.speaker: Unconfirmed speaker
context.intent: Direct the player to the person responsible for work.

legacyEnglish.t000:
ASK AT THE
COUNTER
ABOUT WORK.

findings: The old adaptation is serviceable. Canonical English restores the person being referred to.

records.canonicalEnglish:
Sion: Huh? What's a dead Gigi doing here?
Shoko: Ugh, it's creepy! Hurry up and get rid of it, Sion!
Sion: All right, all right. I get it.

context.speaker: Sion / Shoko
context.intent: Preserve surprise, disgust and Sion's mildly put-upon response.
context.tone: Sion puzzled then put-upon; Shoko disgusted.

legacyEnglish.t009:
HOW CREEPY!
GET RID OF IT,
legacyEnglish.t003:
WHY IS THERE
A DEAD GIGI
HERE?

findings: The draft broadly works, but Shoko's urgency and Sion's resigned response should remain conversational rather than a bare command/acknowledgment.
